newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Indupa to invest $66 mln.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Indupa to invest $66 mln.

text.p: Argentina's Indupa SAIC, controlled by Belgium's Solvay SA, announced Tuesday it will invest $66 million to expand its caustic soda and VCM output.

Indupa, leading local producer of PVC and caustic soda, told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange the investment will be channelled to upgrade its electrolysis and VCM plants in Bahia Blanca, 400 miles (600 kilometres) south of Buenos Aires.
Both projects will be operative around December 1998.
"The investments will allow INDUPA to expand its electrolysis plant caustic soda output to 184,000 tonnes a year while capacity of the VCM plant will be increased to 210,000 tonnes," INDUPA said.
It added increased output will allow it to satisfy increasing domestic demand and strengthen its leading position in the customs union Mercosur, formed by Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay.
